integration_status: Source-level caller and launch connections recorded by reading only; no runtime proof

scope_notes: Public FAST auto names parallel_groves but accepts the compiled resident ordered policy; P01/P03 need the explicit equal-arm OFF prerequisite recorded below
P02 uses ordered resident traversal; P01/P03 use lane-grove traversal. Separate route-specific A/B cells are required, and their combination alone does not prove both routes ran
P04 public class-code entry is FAST and requires the Python parallel_groves engine name; probability-only consumption will miss it
Transient forest_predict_gpu also reaches the shared dispatcher but is not a substitute for public full-workload coverage
No GPU forest extension exists; these shared kernels are compiled into rf and trees
P05 only reaches oblivious models with the equal-arm packed-prediction prerequisite; non-oblivious models retain _apply
P06 also reaches gbdt/train.mojo's shared resident-link launcher, whose grid and block already derive from LINK_BLOCK
Categorical/multiclass/ranking resident callers require their actual full saved recipes; a symmetric regression result alone cannot qualify their outputs
Fit, first prediction and repeated prediction need distinct consumed-output coverage
The saved tree-shap board recipe fits an RF model and consumes explanations; other supported model families need their own full recipes
All direct, leaf-table and decision-table branches share the tile mapping; tail row count is the current chunk rc
P08 includes preparation kernels; P09 can be inert if the existing units cap or small input determines chunk size
P07 keeps the previously losing pair arm and its evidence separate
Training requires the normal DART_DEVICE entry; do not disable it in either arm
Member trees are still trained through rf, so x_trees-only runtime availability is insufficient for full DART fitting
P11 needs both training residual and consumed prediction coverage; P12 only changes the score-add stage after the existing leaf/Newton work

cards.caller_integration: ResidentForest with ordered=False reaches launch_forest_inference[GROVE=True] and _launch_grove_lanes; scalar/vector launch grids, block dimensions and shared reductions use AFT_GROVE_BLOCK/AFT_GROVES_PER_BLOCK together
source_evidence: python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_resident_ordered_flag returns None for FAST parallel_groves, accepting the compiled policy
core/forest_inference_model.mojo:forest_ordered_resident_policy returns not disabled and a supported FAST/IDENTICAL GPU condition; disabled is MOJOLEARN_FOREST_ORDERED_RESIDENT_OFF
core/forest_inference_model.mojo:ResidentForest branches on self.ordered before selecting GROVE=False/True
cards.title: Two logical forest groves per block
cards.mechanism: 64 rather than 128 threads for lane-grove kernels; scratch, item mapping and launch geometry use the same constant.
prerequisites: MOJOLEARN_FOREST_ORDERED_RESIDENT_OFF in both arms for public FAST resident callers
Public inference_engine auto or parallel_groves; no forced row-thread schedule
limitations: Only public callers selecting the grove inference engine reach this candidate.
Existing row-thread schedule overrides still route to their original kernel.

cards.caller_integration: ResidentForest ordered paths and transient GROVE=False callers launch forest_ordered_kernel; dispatcher grid uses AFT_ORDERED_ITEMS and kernel item/second-plane indices use the same row/output tile
source_evidence: core/forest_inference_model.mojo:forest_ordered_resident_policy returns not disabled and ((mode FAST or IDENTICAL) and supported GPU column, or forced IDENTICAL)
python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_resident_ordered_flag returns None for FAST parallel_groves, making the OFF define bypass ordered traversal in the common experiment route
Explicit public inference_engine=sequential can still force ordered traversal, but that is a separate route-specific experiment rather than a P01/P03 combination
cards.title: Paired ordered forest output traversal
affected_estimators: tree wrappers selecting ordered forest inference
cards.mechanism: Two row/output items share the tree loop, with independent ordered accumulators and a guarded second plane.
limitations: Requires ordered inference, not parallel_groves.
Does not change traversal representation or node thresholds.

cards.caller_integration: The public resident OFF prerequisite selects _launch_grove_lanes; forest_grove32_kernel and forest_vector_grove32_kernel allocate the selected capacity and stage rows before their unchanged traversals when feature bytes fit
source_evidence: python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_resident_ordered_flag lets FAST parallel_groves accept that compiled False
core/forest_inference.mojo:launch_forest_inference[GROVE=True] selects _launch_grove_lanes unless the existing row-thread override applies
cards.title: Forest shared rows with a two KiB block budget
cards.mechanism: Enable shared-row staging with capacity derived from 2048 bytes divided by Float32 size and groves per block; overflow rows use direct loads.
prerequisites: MOJOLEARN_FOREST_ORDERED_RESIDENT_OFF in both arms for public FAST resident callers
Public inference_engine auto or parallel_groves; no forced row-thread schedule
limitations: Extends existing staging code with a different storage budget; existing 256-feature staging outcome is not claimed as new evidence.
With P01, per-row capacity increases because fewer rows share the same fixed byte budget.
Scalar-output staging is applicable only to one-output leaves; vector leaves have the existing capacity dispatch.

cards.caller_integration: _predict_forest_labels calls forest_predict_resident_labels_gpu_binding, then resident_predict_labels and ResidentForest's label methods; launch_forest_argmax and forest_argmax_kernel share AFT_ARGMAX_ROWS for complete class-code output coverage
source_evidence: python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_predict_forest_labels returns None unless effective mode is fast and _prediction_engine() is parallel_groves; FAST auto resolves to that name
core/forest_inference_model.mojo:ResidentForest label paths call launch_forest_argmax after either ordered or grove traversal, so the default ordered resident policy does not bypass P04
cards.title: Paired row forest class argmax
cards.mechanism: Two row planes per worker call a shared first-max helper; nonfinite sentinel and class order remain unchanged.
limitations: No effect for regression or raw/probability requests that do not consume class codes.

cards.caller_integration: gbdt_resident_predict_binding reaches _predict_device; GBDT_PREDICT_PACKED with a nonempty oblivious model selects _apply_all. Its grid covers 512 rows/block under P05, matching two 256-lane planes in compute_bins_and_add_all_kernel and its doubled grid stride
cards.title: Two rows reuse packed GBDT split descriptors
cards.mechanism: Each worker loads a tree/split descriptor once for two independent rows; the grid and stride account for two row planes.
limitations: Prerequisite is held equal in both arms; no packed-prediction default is changed.
Non-symmetric fallback keeps its original kernel.
Packed path preparation and its synchronization remain in the future cold-use timed boundary.

cards.caller_integration: Both gbdt/resident_model.mojo and gbdt/train.mojo import LINK_BLOCK and use it in grid construction and resident_link_kernel block_dim; the kernel derives its index/stride from actual block_dim/grid_dim
cards.title: Smaller GBDT resident link block
cards.mechanism: LINK_BLOCK is 128 rather than 256; the existing grid-stride kernel and its callers share the constant.
limitations: Same software binary64 exp/div; this is a scheduling experiment, not reduced precision.
Standalone users of the shared resident-link constant are also affected and need future coverage.

cards.caller_integration: tree_shap_values computes row_units=n_trees*ceil(rc/SHAP_ROW_TILE) for each chunk and uses it for every direct/table/decision-table row launch; each kernel reverses that mapping to the same tree*rc+row unit before calling the original unit implementation
cards.title: TreeSHAP four-row tree tiles
cards.mechanism: Four adjacent rows per tree worker in direct, leaf-table and decision-table paths, with exact row-tail guards.
limitations: Mutually exclusive with MOJOLEARN_SHAP_FAST_ROW_PAIR.
Existing pair audit counter is not used to claim quartet execution.
Sequential unit calls change work mapping; no new persistent model cache is claimed.

cards.caller_integration: shap_prepare, _Forest preparation and tree_shap_values launches use TPB and _grid; kernel _uid or explicit indexing uses that same TPB, including P07/P10 combinations
cards.title: TreeSHAP smaller worker block
cards.mechanism: TPB is 64 rather than 128 for SHAP preparation, table, row and fold kernels.
limitations: Requires full preparation-plus-explanation coverage, not only the row kernel.

cards.caller_integration: tree_shap_values uses _rows_per_chunk(BUF_BYTES) for its contribution allocation and per-iteration rc; it launches and folds every rc-row chunk before advancing r0 by rc
cards.title: TreeSHAP contribution scratch budget
cards.mechanism: Contribution scratch budget becomes 64 MiB instead of 128 MiB, with unchanged per-tree units cap and complete row coverage.
limitations: Can increase chunk count and lose performance; no win claimed.
The full output and leaf table allocations retain existing sizes, so this is not a bound on total GPU memory.

cards.caller_integration: tree_shap_values launches fold_kernel with ceil(fu/AFT_SHAP_FOLD_ITEMS) logical workers; fold_kernel uses TPB*AFT_SHAP_FOLD_ITEMS for each block base and invokes shap_fold_unit for both guarded output-cell planes
cards.title: Paired TreeSHAP output-cell folding
cards.mechanism: Two independent flattened attribution output cells per worker; each still folds every original tree contribution in the original order.
limitations: Refines initial row-tiling idea to output-cell tiling matching the existing fold layout.
No cross-cell reduction or discarded feature attribution.

cards.caller_integration: dart_step launches dart_row_kernel for n rows and dart_predict launches dart_predict_kernel for k*n class/row cells; both callers divide logical work by AFT_DART_ROWS and kernels multiply block bases and capped-grid strides by the same factor
cards.title: Paired DART residual and prediction scheduling
cards.mechanism: Two contiguous lane planes per worker in dart_row_kernel and dart_predict_kernel; launch grids and grid strides use the same tile.
limitations: Dropout draws and unit functions are unchanged.
For prediction a work unit is a class/row cell, not always an entire multiclass row.

cards.caller_integration: dart_add performs existing apply/leaf-sum/Newton work, then launches dart_add_kernel with ceil(n/AFT_DART_ADD_ROWS) logical workers; the kernel applies the original dart_add_unit to the same two row planes and uses a matching multiplied grid stride
cards.title: Paired DART score addition scheduling
cards.mechanism: Two row planes per worker in dart_add_kernel, preserving factor, shrinkage and leaf lookup in the existing unit.
limitations: Does not fuse Newton reduction with score addition or change normalization.
